Designing Linguistic Assertiveness for Robotic Guide-Dog Communication

Graduate research · Sonification Lab · CHI 2027 paper submission
Human-Robot InteractionApplied LLMUser Studies
ProblemHow should a robotic guide dog adapt the assertiveness of its communication across navigation contexts while maintaining clear guidance, user comfort, and agency?
My contributionCo-designed and executed an accessible mixed-methods study with 114 participants examining linguistic assertiveness in robotic guide-dog communication. Developed an LLM-assisted workflow for controlled dialogue stimuli, implemented accessible randomized survey conditions, and analyzed quantitative and qualitative data using ordinal mixed-effects modeling and codebook-based thematic analysis.
ResultCo-authored a CHI 2027 paper submission translating the findings into design guidance for adaptive guide-dog communication.

Game AI: Autonomous Agent Behaviors

Individual course projects · Unity / C#
Unity · C#FSM · Fuzzy LogicProcedural Generation

Individual Unity and C# projects using classic game-AI techniques.

  • Autonomous racecar that steers and controls throttle with fuzzy logic to drive a procedurally generated track (shown), holding above the target speed range with minimal wipeouts.

All agent logic written in C#. These projects earned full marks, with bonus credit for the racecar and dodgeball agents exceeding the assignment's performance targets.
